note: Both spellings of the data directory, always, even here where the fixture's empty home leaves nothing to redirect -- and every other MAVIS_*/MINIMAX_* variable in the parent environment emptied, which is why this list does not name them: MCode reads about ninety, among them three more data directories and four credentials, and overriding one spelling at a time is how MAVIS_DATA_DIR survived into the child in the first place. The data directory moves whether or not a config is written into it, because `orca replay` calls the same `prepare` with the operator's current environment: a fallback that launched MCode untouched ran it on the real ~/.minimax, against the real gateway with the real credential, while the replay saw nothing reach the proxy and reported success. An empty directory of orca's own stops that -- measured, MCode answers `Sign in to MiniMax to use Agent features` and makes no call. Given a config with a custom provider it can prove it rewrote, the adapter also writes a redirected copy into that directory; that path is checked in test/mcode.test.ts, where the file can be read. MCode keeps its origin in that config and uses Node's fetch, which consults neither HTTP_PROXY nor HTTPS_PROXY, so the base-URL route has no variable to set and --tls-intercept sees nothing at all. Verified against @minimax-ai/code 0.4.12 by running it: `orca record mcode -- exec --prompt-mode coding --permission off --max-steps 1 'Reply with exactly: ADAPTER-OK'` recorded 14 events and 6 exchanges, and the request carries a 16,162-character system prompt beginning 'You run inside MiniMax Code, a workspace developed by MiniMax'. The gateway answered 401 -- which is the point: every key orca writes into the generated config is a placeholder, because the file lands inside the run directory and a credential is never written there, and the prompt is captured anyway since it travels in the request. Each custom provider's origin is carried through /forward/ so the call still names the host the operator configured; the run logged upstream=http://155.103.159.98:8317, theirs. Only custom providers can be captured: on that same run MCode rewrote the built-in minimax_api provider's baseURL and apiKey on startup, restoring its own values -- the apiKey as the literal sk-xxx from its bundle, not the operator's, measured against a config whose every key had been replaced by a distinct canary.
